::: {#def-min-max-scaling}
#### Min-max scaling

Let $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ be observations of a variable
with minimum $x_{\min}$ and maximum $x_{\max} > x_{\min}$.
The **min-max scaled value** of $x_i$ is

$$\frac{x_i - x_{\min}}{x_{\max} - x_{\min}}$$

:::

::: notes
Every min-max scaled value lies in $[0, 1]$:
the minimum maps to $0$ and the maximum maps to $1$.
Min-max scaling is sensitive to outliers.
If one district's median income of 100 were recorded by mistake
among values ranging from 0 to 15,
min-max scaling would squeeze all the other values into $[0, 0.15]$,
while [standardization](#def-standardization) would change them far less
[@geron2017hands, chapter 2, "Feature Scaling"].
:::
